item.title: Kwon Eunbi & Heo Yong Joon on the Long Game, Chapters Left Behind and the Beginning of Something Greater
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we're celebrating the upcoming 2026 FIFA World Cup. As part of Billboard's Global World Cup Series, we're pairing top soccer stars with talented musicians from around the world. Today, we're shining the spotlight on South Korea, a team that's been making waves in the soccer world for decades.
[Soft music transitions]
Host: This summer, the World Cup is bigger than ever, with 48 teams competing across three host nations: the United States, Canada, and Mexico. South Korea is making its 11th consecutive appearance, and the nation is ready to come together to cheer on their team. As singer Kwon Eunbi puts it, "Oh Pilseung Korea" - a chant that unites tens of thousands of strangers into a single voice.
[Short music clip: "Underwater" by Kwon Eunbi]
Host: Kwon Eunbi is a talented singer who's already made a name for herself in the music industry. She's known for her hit single "Underwater," which became a delayed hit after a show-stopping performance at the 2023 Waterbomb festival. She's now signed with RBW, the label behind MAMAMOO and ONEWE, and is ready to take on new challenges.
[Short music clip: stadium ambiance]
Host: On the soccer field, we have Heo Yong Joon, a skilled striker who's been making waves in the K League. Fans call him "Heonaldo" for his impressive goals and celebrations. He's been working towards his goal of playing abroad, and we can't wait to see what the future holds for him.
[Soft music transitions]
Host: We had the chance to sit down with Kwon Eunbi and talk about what it means to be part of this project. She shared with us, "I think music and sports are deeply alike in the way they bring people's emotions together. The World Cup especially is such a special event - people all over the world cheering together in the same moment."
[Short clip: Kwon Eunbi speaking]
Kwon Eunbi: "For me, the World Cup brings back memories of the whole family gathering in front of the TV to cheer together. When I was little, I remember watching the matches with my family in a Red Devils T-shirt - and I can still vividly picture the excitement and joy of those moments."
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. We're excited to see what the future holds for Kwon Eunbi and Heo Yong Joon, and we can't wait to cheer on the South Korean team in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Join us next time for more exciting stories and interviews.
